title: Informal Conjecture (chordal modulator characterization for even-hole-free graphs)
statement_text: Every chordal graph of clique number at most three modulates even-hole-free graphs.
context_text: Containment means as an induced subgraph. A hole is an induced cycle of length at least four, and a graph is even-hole-free if it has no hole of even length; a chordal graph is a graph with no hole. A $t$-basic obstruction is one of $K_t$, $K_{t,t}$, a subdivision of the $(t\times t)$-wall, or the line graph of such a subdivision, and a graph is $t$-clean if it contains no $t$-basic obstruction. A graph $H$ modulates a class $\mathcal{G}$ if for every positive integer $t$ there is $w(t)$ such that every $t$-clean $H$-free graph in $\mathcal{G}$ has treewidth at most $w(t)$. For even-hole-free graphs, being $t$-clean is equivalent to being $K_t$-free, so $H$ modulates even-hole-free graphs iff for every $t$, even-hole-free graphs with no $H$ and no clique of size $t$ have bounded treewidth. Sintiari and Trotignon constructed (even-hole, $K_4$)-free graphs of arbitrarily large treewidth and with no short holes (layered wheels), which shows that a graph $H$ can modulate even-hole-free graphs only if $H$ is chordal with clique number at most three; the authors say the converse may also be true. They prove the case of clique number at most two, i.e. every forest modulates even-hole-free graphs, and they show that forests are exactly the graphs modulating the larger class of (theta, prism)-free graphs. Extending to all chordal graphs of clique number at most three remains open.
notes: Stated as "as far as we know, the converse may also be true" in the introduction; confirmed open by the subsequent remark "while the former remains open".
paper_title: Induced subgraphs and tree decompositions VIII. Excluding a forest in (theta, prism)-free graphs
